title: The cognitive-motor link is mostly age, certified: adjusting for age attenuates the sway-cognition correlation from 0.53 to 0.20 (partial correlation to machine precision vs ppcor)

dataset.name: BDS -- a public data set of human balance evaluations (Santos & Duarte 2016)
dataset.record: per subject: eyes-closed-foam COP path length (cm), Trail Making Test A time (s), age (years); n=158
dataset.citation: Santos DA, Duarte M. A public data set of human balance evaluations. PeerJ 2016;4:e2648. doi:10.7717/peerj.2648.

proposition: The sibling case found a cognitive-motor association -- slower processing speed tracks more postural sway (Spearman rho = 0.532) -- but flagged age as a shared correlate. Adjusting for age answers whether the link is real. Each subject's sway comes from the certified swayMetrics; the NEWLY-AUTHORED partialCorrelation computes the rank partial correlation of sway and Trail Making Test A controlling for age, reproducing the ppcor package AND an independent closed-form recompute to machine precision. The association ATTENUATES to a rank partial correlation of 0.201 (p=0.012, still significant but much weaker), and the linear (Pearson) partial correlation vanishes (0.048, p=0.55): most of the marginal link was age, though a modest rank association survives.

validation.reference: The newly-authored partialCorrelation op (Pearson or rank/Spearman, controlling for covariate[s] by residualising on [1, z] via QR) is validated against BOTH the ppcor package (ppcor::pcor.test) AND an independent closed-form recompute (the correlation-matrix formula) on the identical (sway, TMT-A, age) triples -- a double reference. All agree to machine precision (|diff| ~ 2e-16 vs ppcor; the Pearson partial is bit-for-bit vs the closed-form, |diff| = 0). The per-subject eyes-closed-foam sway comes from PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics (path_length, certified against Prieto in the sibling sway-posturography-bds case).
validation.data: REAL -- Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS; eyes-closed-foam COP path length, Trail Making Test A time, age; n=158
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) partialCorrelation reproduces ppcor::pcor.test and an independent closed-form recompute to machine precision; (2) the cognitive-motor association is largely age-confounded. HONEST scope: (1) this AUTHORS A NEW OP, partialCorrelation (Pearson or rank/Spearman, controlling for covariate[s] by residualising on [1, z] via QR), and reuses the certified swayMetrics op for the eyes-closed-foam sway; (2) the partial correlation reproduces the ppcor package (ppcor::pcor.test) AND an independent closed-form recompute to MACHINE PRECISION (|diff| ~ 2e-16 vs each; the Pearson partial is bit-for-bit vs the closed-form, |diff| = 0); (3) the finding: the cognitive-motor association is LARGELY AGE-CONFOUNDED -- the rank partial correlation ATTENUATES from the marginal Spearman rho of 0.532 to 0.201 (p = 0.012, still significant but much weaker) after adjusting for age, while the LINEAR partial correlation VANISHES (Pearson 0.048, p = 0.55); so a modest rank association survives age adjustment -- consistent with a small direct cognitive-motor contribution to standing balance -- but most of the marginal link was shared age variance; (4) this honestly RESOLVES the sibling sway-cognition-kendall-bds case's open question (the association is real but mostly age); (5) a cross-sectional ASSOCIATION, NOT causation; adjusting for one covariate does not rule out others; one per-subject value; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: Adjusting for age leaves a modest but significant rank partial correlation (0.20); whether this reflects a direct cognitive-motor pathway (executive/attentional control of posture) or residual confounding by other age-linked factors (medication, comorbidity, sensory loss) needs a fuller multivariable model and, ideally, a dual-task or longitudinal design. The single-covariate partial correlation shown here is the honest first adjustment. Documented, not escalated.
